newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAEL KNESSET PANEL APPROVES 1997 BUDGET CUT.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL KNESSET PANEL APPROVES 1997 BUDGET CUT.

text.p: The Israeli parliament's finance committee approved on Wednesday, by a majority of one, an 800 million shekel ($226.6 million) cut in the government's 1997 budget, the committee secretary said.
The cut is needed to enable the government to meet its 1997 budget deficit target of 2.8 percent of gross domestic product, or 9.7 billion shekels, excluding credit.
The 800 million shekel cut affects all ministry budgets with the lion's share coming from defence and education spending.

On Sunday, Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman withdrew the proposal to cut the budget when it became clear it was not going to pass because of objections from some coalition members to cuts in the education and social welfare budgets. He resubmitted the proposal to the committee on Wednesday.
The budget cut already has received cabinet approval and the finance committee's vote was the final hurdle.
The 800 million shekel cut is in addition to seven billion shekels in cuts and revenue raising measures already implemented.
